title: A Survey of Large Language Models for Financial Applications: Progress, Prospects and Challenges
authors: Yuqi Nie, Yaxuan Kong, Xiaowen Dong, John M. Mulvey, H. Vincent Poor, Qingsong Wen, Stefan Zohren
venue: arXiv preprint (submitted to Journal of Machine Learning), 2025
tldr: A comprehensive survey of LLMs in finance covering 500+ papers across linguistic tasks, sentiment analysis, time series forecasting, financial reasoning, and agent-based modeling with a unified evaluation framework and public repository.
problem_and_motivation: Finance generates vast unstructured text data (news, reports, transcripts) but traditional NLP models struggle with domain-specific terminology, temporal context, and complex reasoning. Foundation models offer new capabilities but face challenges in hallucination, domain adaptation, and data pollution. A systematic survey is needed to map progress and open challenges.
approach: Systematic literature review covering over 500 papers (2020-2024) on LLMs for financial applications.
Five-category taxonomy of financial tasks: Financial Linguistic Tasks, Financial Sentiment Analysis, Financial Time Series, Financial Reasoning, Financial Agent-based Modeling.
Comprehensive collection of publicly available datasets, benchmarks, and model checkpoints in a unified GitHub repository.

Evaluation framework categorizing human-centered vs. outcome-based metrics across six dimensions: Fluency, Factuality, Faithfulness, Conciseness, Domain-specific applicability, and Downstream task performance.
Analysis of base architectures: BERT, RoBERTa, ELECTRA, T5, and GPT-family variants adapted to finance.
Domain-specific model survey: FinBERT, BloombergGPT, FinMA, FinGPT, XuanYuan, CFGPT, and others.
Analysis of key challenges: lookahead bias, legal implications, data pollution, signal decay, and interpretability.
findings: cat: Financial LLMs are categorized into base model improvements (retraining, domain-adaptive pretraining), post-processing improvements (RAG, prompt engineering, fine-tuning), and evaluation.
cat: FinBERT and its derivatives (FinBERT-FL, FineFinBERT) remain dominant for sentiment analysis with state-of-the-art performance on FiQA, Financial PhraseBank, and FP datasets.
cat: BloombergGPT (50B, trained on Bloomberg's financial data) excels on financial tasks but underperforms on general NLP benchmarks vs. LLaMA2-70B.
cat: FinMA (series from 7B to 70B) uses LLaMA and Mistral as base models with instruction tuning for universal financial task coverage.
num: ChatGPT achieved 74.2% accuracy on FinQA, outperforming fine-tuned models without explicit training on financial data.
cat: Financial time series forecasting increasingly uses LLMs as feature extractors (LLM4TS, FinTime) and as generative forecasters.
cat: LLM-based agents (FinMem, FinAgent, FinChain) combine LLMs with tools for automated financial analysis and trading.

cat: Key challenges include lookahead bias in training data, legal liability for AI-generated advice, data pollution from overlapping benchmarks, signal decay in trading strategies, and lack of interpretability.

definitions.definition: A type of data leakage where financial training data inadvertently incorporates future information, inflating model performance metrics.
The phenomenon where financial predictive signals diminish over time as market participants adapt to and arbitrage away systematic patterns.
An LLM-based autonomous system that can reason about financial data, make decisions, and execute actions in financial environments.
Continued pretraining of a general-purpose LLM on a domain-specific corpus to adapt its knowledge and vocabulary to finance.

topics.name: Financial Text Mining and Analysis
topics.justification: Core survey focus on financial NLP: summarization, report generation, information extraction from financial documents.

topics.name: AI/ML Model Development and Evaluation

topics.name: AI Explainability and Interpretability

topics.name: Foundation Models and Transfer Learning

topics.name: Data Quality and Bias
topics.justification: Extensive discussion of data pollution, lookahead bias, benchmark contamination, and data quality challenges.

topics.name: Financial Advisory and Decision Support Systems

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides the most comprehensive systematic survey (500+ papers) of LLM applications in finance with a unified taxonomy, evaluation framework, and curated repository of datasets, models, and benchmarks.
directly_justifies: Odin's use of LLMs and foundation models for financial applications needs to account for domain adaptation strategies.
RAG and prompt engineering are viable approaches for financial text tasks.
Lookahead bias and data pollution are critical concerns for any financial ML system.
Financial agent architectures combining LLMs with tools are a promising direction.
limits: Survey nature; does not contribute new models or empirical results.
Coverage up to early 2024; rapidly evolving field may have newer advancements.
Evaluation framework is proposed but not validated against practitioners.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Comprehensive survey of algorithmic LLM methods for finance. Covers forecasting, text mining, ML development, and explainability.

limitations: Survey covers literature only up to early 2024; the field evolves rapidly.
Proposed evaluation framework is conceptual and not empirically validated.
Does not provide direct model comparisons on identical benchmarks (heterogeneous evaluation settings across papers).
Potential selection bias toward English-language financial LLM research.
remember_this: 500+ papers surveyed; unified taxonomy across 5 financial task categories.
FinBERT remains dominant for sentiment analysis; BloombergGPT excels at finance but lags on general tasks.
Key challenges: lookahead bias, data pollution, signal decay, legal liability, interpretability.
FinMA, FinGPT, and financial agents (FinMem, FinAgent) are state-of-the-art directions.
Evaluation framework: Fluency, Factuality, Faithfulness, Conciseness, Domain applicability, Downstream performance.
